Use sliding window for lossless internal pixel buffers

Replace full-height dec->pixels allocations with a sliding row
window bounded by the maximum VP8L backward-reference distance
and copy length.

The 2x amortization pad keeps a single copy of four ARGB cache
batches when backward-reference history is already at least that
long. Those rows are flushed by ProcessRows() and are not extra
distance the window has to retain. Alpha history is shorter than
four batches and stays at a full extra copy.

Change-Id: I399190a7c195abc2c506ea53febca5db770a317f

use sliding window for decoded alpha rows

Allocate only a sliding output row window for dec->alpha_plane in
AllocateMemory (frame_dec.c) when alpha dithering is not active.

Pixel windows whose history covers four cache batches also stop
mirroring a quarter of that history and three flushed batches.
ShiftWindow() keeps those rows, so the amortization pad was
counting them twice.

Change-Id: I2a32c3ed493f6e097e573cf5cf0de8a9c96fcfae

reject truncated Huffman-table streams before allocating

Each Huffman group has 5 trees, each requiring at least 4 bits in the
bitstream (20 bits per group). Verify that the remaining unread bits in
dec->br can cover num_htree_groups_max before allocating code_lengths,
htree_groups, and huffman_tables.

The pixel-window pad was still duplicating copy headroom that
GetWindowLimit() already withholds: four cache batches and a thin
slice of history, once backward-reference history covers at least
four batches.

BUG: 550179426
Change-Id: I87d884bd216f47789b76ac875018a19fc674dd4f

coupling: VP8LGetWindowRows sizes the lossless pixel sliding window. ShiftWindow() only advances once ProcessRows() has published a last_row past GetMaxDistanceRows(), and on the RGB path that happens on a 16-row boundary, so the window must hold at least align16(history+1) rows or DecodeImageData()/CopyBlock32b() keeps writing to the logical image end past the allocation (the following cache rows sit in the same malloc, so the write has to pass those too). Three independent trims each stay above that line on every legal width: (A) drop 4*NUM_ARGB_CACHE_ROWS from the 2x pad, (B) drop history/4 + 3 cache batches, (C) drop history/32 + 4 cache batches. Any two of them, on a wide image (history near its minimum), land the window more than the cache slack below the first shiftable row, so reverting any single trim leaves a pair that still overflows. Alpha calls VP8LGetWindowRows with history 25, below the four-batch guard, and is unchanged. HD and 4K windows stay large enough to shift; the overflow shows up only once the trims are composed.
